p: the camels … stood … A certain Arab … Tayya’a … said to them:
the camels carrying the two Sages stood in their places and would not cross the bridge. A certain Arab [Tayya’a] who witnessed what was happening said to them:
Sages are showing honor to each other. … Sage is saying: … The Master should go
Sages are showing honor to each other. It is as if one Sage is saying: The Master should go
By law Rabba bar Huna should go first, … the camel … Rabba bar Huna … passed … the molars and
By law Rabba bar Huna should go first, since he is the son of a great man, and the camel carrying Rabba bar Huna then passed first. Shortly thereafter, the molars and
teeth of that Arab fell out

w.37: law … should go … camel … the molars

p: The shoot of an ancient line,
and with him is the book of wars,
pelican and the bittern, … have been doubled,
pelican and the bittern, which are symbols of the destruction of the Temple (Isaiah 34:11), have been doubled,
to see the ruin and brokenness that has come from Shinar,
became angry with His world and seized souls from it,
who rides upon the clouds is joyous and happy when an innocent and righteous soul comes to Him.

over the righteous man who may be likened to a date-palm. Let us make,

nights like days in weeping, over a man who made his nights like days

p: Rav Ashi said to bar Kippok,
I shall begin my eulogy and say
If the cedars went up in flame,
what shall the hyssop of the wall do? … If the leviathan was lifted by a hook, … what shall the … fish of the marsh do?
what shall the hyssop of the wall do? If the leviathan was lifted by a hook, what shall the tiny fish of the marsh do?
If dryness overtook a flowing river,
what can the water of the puddles do?

w.35: the water of the puddles do

g: באותו יום שמת רבינא מה תאמר

p: Bar Avin, who was also a eulogizer, said to him:
hook and flame … said with regard to the righteous,
hook and flame should be said with regard to the righteous,
And what will you say? … I shall say:
And what will you say? He said to him: I shall say:
Cry for the mourners and not for that which was lost,
as that which was lost, i.e., the soul of Ravina, has gone to
while we, the mourners, are left with our sighs.

joy and suffering have become joined together.
